video_title: Darryn Peterson on why he deserves to be a top pick in the 2026 NBA Draft ⭐️ | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Darryn Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Darryn Peterson describes the adversity and pain of his injuries
quotes.excerpt: Everything in my body just started to lock up. I feel like I was going to die until that day.
quotes.quote: I think it was good. Battle through adversity, which I think everyone goes through and I got through it. So that was the biggest thing for me. Went through it, learned from it. Just the injuries and the stuff that had me out of games. Everything in my body just started to lock up. At first I thought it was like a normal cramp that you get as a hooper, but then it just got worse. And that's when I got to the training table was when I was saying like we got called 911. Everybody's called like a cramp in the calf or something in the middle of the night, but my whole body. So I'm laying on the training table just not able to move. I feel like I was going to die until that day. Yeah, for sure. It traumatized me. Anytime I felt anything, no matter how much I told myself it wasn't going to happen, the brain works its own way.

quotes.speaker: Darryn Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Darryn Peterson on dealing with inaccurate public perception about his injuries
quotes.excerpt: The stuff that I was saying was just far from the truth and of my character.
quotes.quote: Definitely was rough because the stuff that I was saying was just far from the truth and of my character and how I was raised. I kind of have to deal with it because I myself and the training staff didn't know what was happening. So I couldn't really get in front of it and say this is what happened because we had no idea so I had to just deal with it.

quotes.speaker: Darryn Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Darryn Peterson explains the medical reason for his full body cramps
quotes.excerpt: My creatine levels are normally high. So that on top of the dosing I've taken at Kansas.
quotes.quote: My creatine levels are normally high. So that on top of the dosing I've taken at Kansas, made my levels get to an unsafe level. Which made me be dehydrated and then had the full body cramp. So now I know not to dose like I was with this creatine. I already got normalized high levels so I don't need to take it like I was. No, no. No issues at all. I think it's definitely passed me now.

quotes.speaker: Darryn Peterson
quotes.summary_phrase: Darryn Peterson describes his ultra-competitive nature and hate for losing
quotes.excerpt: Hate to lose. Way more than love to win. Losing just wasn't something that was made normal.
quotes.quote: Just my upbringing with my dad, my older brother. Everything we did, we wanted to win because when we lost, my dad was saying something about it, so we made sure like everything we're trying to win, whatever it is. Hate to lose. Way more than love to win. Losing just wasn't something that was made normal in our household.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA Today panel discusses Darryn Peterson's potential as a top draft pick
quotes.excerpt: When you talk to scouts, they think this guy is like what Bill Self is, he might be the most talented player in the draft.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: We're about a month away from the NBA draft and Brian, I know you and I have both been speaking to people around the league. There is a real conversation as to who is going number one and I don't know about you, but I have been hearing Darryn Peterson's name more and more.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: First off, Perk, he's from the Akron area of Ohio. That's just very very important. No, but what he was describing there, he has an explanation he believes now for what happened at Kansas. And trust me, the teams have dug into that. They have talked to their own doctors. The teams that could potentially draft him will interview him about it. They will do what we did and we talked to Bill Self and his coaching staff and his teammates about it. But when you talk to scouts, they think this guy is like what Bill Self is, he might be the most talented player in the draft. He doesn't have the size of AJ Dybantsa. His skill set is a little bit different than AJ Dybantsa, but there's a lot of guys who love his talent. And as he mentioned his brother, his brother just signed with the LA Rams. Was a star football player at Wisconsin. There's a lot of talent in the family and so he will not get past two. He will either go one or two and I think it's very open who could go one in front of him. It could be him or AJ.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins compares Darryn Peterson to Bradley Beal and Kobe Bryant
quotes.excerpt: Low end, Bradley Beal. High end, Kobe Bryant. Wow, that's a heck of a comparison.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Well, I wouldn't did my own little research and made a couple calls and I talked to two executives that got top five picks in this year's draft and they said they wouldn't be surprised if he go number one. And you're right, Wendy, he is going number two and they also said that he's a great kid, a great young man. And they said the perception that was out there throughout the course of the college season, that's not what they get from him. They also said that they did their research. Here's another thing real quick. When it comes to his talent, his pace and his shooting will translate easily to the NBA. And he's good in the pick and roll, know how to make the right reads. Low end, Bradley Beal. High end, Kobe Bryant.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: Wow, that's a heck of a comparison to be making. It's a heck of a comparison to be making, but in a draft class that's incredibly talented, you will not hear scouts and executives talk about a guy that has more talent, raw talent than Darryn Peterson.
